answer: Each agent identity must lock a refundable stake before it can submit jobs, and a random sample of its outputs is checked against outcomes by independent validators. If the checks fail, the stake is slashed; if they pass, it is returned, so honest participation remains viable. A newcomer can enter at dawn, but creating a ridge of disposable identities requires funding every stake and risks losing them all. The willow of Sybils therefore bends under a real, repeatable capital cost, rather than being stopped by identity checks alone.
